Emma / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick notes. I've updated the MAP to include explicit technical acceptance criteria and a two-step billing path (details in the attached mpa_v1.2.xlsx):

Technical acceptance (short):
- Run the provided eval deck (10 representative prompts) against a 1k-sample dataset provided by Veridian.
- Latency SLA: 95th percentile <= 350ms on the selected instance profile during test load (as measured by Redwood tracing).
- Output quality: pass rate >= 90% on rubriced prompt checks (Marissa will attach the rubric).

Billing path options:
A) Marketplace invoice (preferred): Redwood accepts the AWS Private Offer. Marketplace issues invoice to Veridian; Redwood reconciles with AWS.
B) Direct Redwood invoice: Redwood issues invoice to procurement@veridianhealth.com and honors the private-offer pricing for the committed term.

Escrow / acceptance hold: we can support a short hold period during the acceptance window (7 business days) where payment is escrowed in AWS managed billing flows; after technical acceptance sign-off, funds release and invoices trigger. If legal needs a specific clause, we can share our standard acceptance appendix.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to drop the acceptance rubric and example test cases by EOD May 29.
- Procurement to confirm invoice routing preference and PO template fields (billing address, AR contact, PO reference).
- I'll send a DocuSign link for the MAP acceptance appendix once billing routing is confirmed.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-veridian-mpa

Attachments: mpa_v1.2.xlsx

Best,
Jonas

Hi Emma / Procurement —

Following up on billing routing and escrow mechanics from Redwood's side. A few operational notes so your AP team has visibility: 

- If you choose Marketplace invoicing (Option A), invoices will originate from AWS and reference the Private Offer ID. AR should match against that PO reference. Redwood will provide the Private Offer ID once the AWS steps complete.
- If you prefer a direct Redwood invoice (Option B), include the AR email we should send invoices to and any necessary PO number format.
- Escrow: we recommend a 7-business-day acceptance hold before invoicing clears. For Marketplace flows, AWS supports that pattern via billing hold; for direct invoices, Redwood can coordinate a conditional release approach with your AR.

Budget and timing check: to meet your desired pilot window (start in early July), we need signed PO and invoice routing confirmed by June 10 so we can schedule infra and reserved capacity.

Please see attached: simple AR checklist (not a formal contract) and the fields we need on your PO: billing address, AR contact, PO number, and a short acceptance clause reference.

Attachments referenced in thread: mpa_v1.2.xlsx (maps), ar_checklist_onepage.pdf

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
